cards.text: The church in Jerusalem is growing faster than dough in a warm kitchen. Two groups of Jewish believers are part of it, the Grecian Jews and the Hebraic Jews, and every day there's a distribution of food. Then the grumbling starts.

cards.question: The Grecian Jews start grumbling against the Hebraic Jews. What's their complaint?

answers.text: Their homes are too far from the temple
Their language is left out of the prayers

cards.text: So the Twelve, Jesus' apostles, summon all the disciples to one big meeting. I could never even get the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with to come to a meeting, and they had NOWHERE else to be.

cards.question: The Twelve say it's unacceptable for them to wait on tables if it means neglecting something. What is it?

cards.text: So the Twelve tell the disciples to pick some men from among themselves, and the Twelve will hand this job to them. Smart, because the one time I stamped dough with one end of my mustache and pulled a tray with the other, the cookies came out fine and my mustache came out SMOKED.

cards.question: The Twelve ask the disciples to select ___ men for the job.
Not just anybody, either. The men handing out the food must be confirmed to be full of the ___ and ___.
Once the seven take over the food, what will the Twelve devote themselves to?

answers.text: Prayer and the ministry of the word

cards.text: This proposal pleased the whole group. A whole crowd agreeing on one plan? I can't get two cookies on the same tray to agree on which end is warmer.

cards.question: The first man they choose is described as full of faith and of the Holy Spirit. Who is he?

cards.text: Then come Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch, a convert to Judaism. I tried saying those six names fast, made it as far as Prochorus, and had to go sit down by the oven.

cards.question: When the seven are presented to the apostles, the apostles anoint them with oil.

cards.text: The apostles pray and lay their hands on the seven. So the word of God continued to spread, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly.

cards.question: Among the new believers in Jerusalem, a great number of priests became obedient to the faith.

cards.text: Now the spotlight turns to Stephen, one of the seven. He's full of grace and power, and he's performing great wonders and signs among the people.

But resistance comes from what was called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, with Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and men from the provinces of Cilicia and Asia, and they dispute with Stephen. One man against all THAT is not a debate, friend, that's a line at my bakery counter where everybody took a number.

cards.question: The men from the Synagogue of the Freedmen take Stephen on in a debate. How does it go?

answers.text: They can't stand up to his wisdom
They trip him up with the law
They walk off without a word

cards.text: They can't stand up to his wisdom or the Spirit by whom he spoke. That's me arguing with my oven timer: I make GREAT points, and it just keeps counting down.

cards.question: The men from the synagogue can't win the debate against Stephen. What do they do next?

answers.text: Get some men to accuse him
Ask the apostles to quiet him

cards.question: The men claim they heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against ___ and against God.

cards.text: So they stirred up the people, elders, and scribes and confronted Stephen. The people, the elders AND the scribes, all for one man? That's a lot of backup for a guy who just won a debate.

cards.question: They seize Stephen and bring him before the ___.

cards.text: Now Stephen stands before the Sanhedrin, Israel's ruling council. And there they present false witnesses.

cards.question: In front of the Sanhedrin, what do the false witnesses say Stephen never stops speaking against?
The false witnesses claim Stephen said he would destroy the holy place himself.

cards.text: Their claim is that he said Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses handed down. Then everyone sitting in the Sanhedrin looks intently at Stephen.

cards.question: Every eye in the Sanhedrin is on Stephen, and they see that his face is like the face of ___.

cards.text: A face like an angel's, in a room full of accusers. That's where we'll leave Stephen for now, friend, because his story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The joke invents a customer line at his bakery counter where everybody takes a number. In his story he lives on the cookie planet alone and invites bakers to help, so a line of customers adds something new to his world. The comparison also misses the action. A take-a-number line is people waiting their turn to be served, not a group arguing against one man.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The oven timer joke doesn't match the action. In Acts 6:10 the opponents can't stand up to Stephen's wisdom and the Spirit he speaks by. In the joke, a timer just ignores Papa Dorin's points and keeps counting down. Ignoring an argument isn't the same as answering it with wisdom.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card tells that Stephen is before the Sanhedrin, which comes from Acts 6:12, and that false witnesses are presented, which comes from Acts 6:13. It cites only Acts 6:13. The citation should be Acts 6:12-13.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer says "The temple and the law," but Acts 6:13 says "this holy place and against the law." The next card, card 11, uses "holy place," so the two cards call the same thing by different names.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the exact wording of the line "his face was like the face of an angel." Card 12 only says the council looks intently at Stephen. Nothing before this card lets the baker reason toward "an angel" over "a prophet" or "a lion," so getting it right is luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card calls the Sanhedrin "a room full of accusers." Acts 6:13-15 says false witnesses were presented and that everyone sitting in the Sanhedrin looked intently at Stephen. It never calls the whole council accusers.
